name: x402stock News Sentiment
description: Global news attention and tone for any company, ticker, or topic, from the GDELT Project's worldwide news monitoring: an average/latest tone score with a positive/neutral/negative label and trend, an hourly tone timeline, an article-volume timeline, and recent headlines. Verified with q='Nvidia', timespan='1w': sentiment {latest_tone:0.951, average_tone:0.639, label:'neutral', trend:'worsening'}.

q.description: Company name, ticker, or free-text topic to search news tone/attention for, e.g. 'Nvidia', 'AAPL', 'inflation'. QUERY parameter, required.

inputSchema.description: GET query parameters (not path segments, unlike x402stock's ticker-in-path endpoints). No request body.

outputSchema.description: Flat JSON envelope: a sentiment summary, a volume summary, an hourly tone_timeline, an optional volume_timeline, and recent_articles headlines.

sentiment.description: latest_tone, average_tone (GDELT tone units, roughly -10 very negative to +10 very positive, 0 neutral; both nullable when no coverage), label (positive|neutral|negative), trend, scale (human-readable scale legend)

volume.description: total_articles, points — observed 0/0 in the verified call even though tone_timeline had data; do not assume non-zero

tone_timeline.description: hourly {date, tone} points over the requested timespan

volume_timeline.description: {date, articles, total_monitored} points — observed empty([]) in the verified call

recent_articles.description: {title, url, domain, source_country, language, seen}, each field nullable — observed empty([]) in the verified call

usage.callShape: GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/news-sentiment?q={query}&timespan={span} — q (required, free-text company/ticker/topic, 2-120 chars) and timespan (optional enum 1d|3d|1w|2w|1m|3m, default '1w') are QUERY parameters, not path segments. No request body. x402 'exact' USDC payment on Base (eip155:8453); the identical path/params/price are also servable directly at https://x402stock.xyz/api/v1/news-sentiment.
usage.outputShape: body.sentiment.{latest_tone,average_tone,label,trend,scale} (tone fields nullable); body.volume.{total_articles,points}; body.tone_timeline[] of {date,tone}; body.volume_timeline[] of {date,articles,total_monitored}; body.recent_articles[] of {title,url,domain,source_country,language,seen}; plus body.source('x402stock'), body.venue('gdelt'), body.query, body.timespan, body.as_of, body.attribution.
quirks: q is a QUERY parameter (?q=Nvidia), unlike sibling x402stock endpoints (quote/snapshot) which take the ticker as a URL PATH segment.
q accepts a free-text company name, ticker, OR topic — not restricted to US-listed tickers.
timespan is optional (default '1w'); enum 1d|3d|1w|2w|1m|3m.

Data source is the GDELT Project's global news-tone monitoring — explicitly described by the provider as 'distinct from the Reddit/4chan feeds' (x402stock's separate /trending/reddit and /trending/4chan endpoints).

In the verified call (q=Nvidia, timespan=1w) tone_timeline was well populated (165 hourly points spanning 2026-07-23T06:00Z–2026-07-30T04:00Z, with exactly 2 hourly buckets missing from that span: 2026-07-26T02:00Z and 2026-07-26T05:00Z) but volume.total_articles and volume.points were both 0, and volume_timeline/recent_articles were both empty arrays — the tone series and the volume/article-listing parts of the payload can be inconsistent for the same query; do not assume article listings will be present just because tone data is.
sentiment.latest_tone/average_tone are nullable (anyOf number|null) per the schema when there is no recent coverage for the query.
Fixed price ($0.02, meterSlug 'news_sentiment', serviceSlug 'sentiment-positioning'), not a dynamic/ceiling charge.

The 402 challenge's payTo escrow address is minted fresh per request by x402stock's ZeroClick/Stripe-backed payment proxy — two probes of this exact URL returned two different payTo values (0x70fdfcfe2d90287766fda5bf10b7dfa942532429 captured at the paid call; 0x195eaeb803f9bf199a667f892e0cbf056e844873 on a later unpaid re-probe), each internally consistent between the base64 payment-required header and the JSON body. Always pay the payTo/accepts from the CURRENT 402, never a cached one.

Same provider is reachable at two hosts with identical paths/params/price/response bodies: agents.x402stock.xyz (this backend — offers both x402 and MPP; x402 'exact' on Base confirmed live) and x402stock.xyz directly (x402 only, per its own llms.txt).
usage.guide: Call GET https://agents.x402stock.xyz/api/v1/news-sentiment with a required `q` query parameter (a company name, ticker, or free-text topic, e.g. 'Nvidia') and an optional `timespan` query parameter (one of 1d/3d/1w/2w/1m/3m, default '1w'). Pay $0.02 in USDC via x402 'exact' on Base — no API key, no sign-in. The 200 response is flat JSON: read body.sentiment for the average/latest GDELT tone score (roughly -10 very negative to +10 very positive, 0 neutral) with a positive/neutral/negative label and trend, body.tone_timeline[] for the hourly tone series, body.volume / body.volume_timeline for article counts, and body.recent_articles[] for headlines. In testing, the tone series was populated while the volume/article-count/headline fields were all empty for the same query — treat those as possibly empty even when tone data exists. Data is GDELT global news-tone monitoring, distinct from x402stock's Reddit/4chan trending-ticker endpoints.

name: SignalFuse Macro Regime
description: Classifies the current macro market regime as risk-on, risk-off, or neutral with a directional classification (bullish/bearish/neutral), a 0-1 confidence score, and a short reasoning string; a no-input GET that returns the latest crypto-macro read.

inputSchema.description: No input parameters — call without query params.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/regime (no query params, no path params, no body). Pay the x402 quote ($0.001 USDC on Base eip155:8453); the result returns inline in the 200 JSON.
usage.outputShape: regime (enum: risk_on|risk_off|neutral), classification (enum: bullish|bearish|neutral), confidence (number 0-1), reasoning (string), updated_at (ISO date-time), related[] ({path, price, why} pointers to other SignalFuse endpoints).
quirks: No inputs at all — it's a single global macro read, not per-symbol (unlike the /v1/signal/{symbol} and /v1/sentiment/{symbol} siblings).

STALE/DECAYED STATE: when no fresh signal exists the API still returns 200 (paid) with regime='neutral', confidence=0, reasoning='Decayed — last signal was N.Nh ago'. Verified live response was exactly this decayed state, so the advertised populated example (risk_on / 0.82 / BTC-momentum reasoning) was NOT observed in this run.
x402 payment settled ($0.001 USDC on Base) but confirmed:false and no txHash was returned by the payment layer.
A free downgrade exists at GET /v1/regime/preview (regime + confidence, no reasoning); this paid endpoint adds the reasoning string.

Alt access without a wallet: POST /v1/credits/trial {wallet} grants 5 free credits (x-credit-token header), or the browser playground at signalfuse.co/play (25 free calls/day). Not used here — indexed via x402.
usage.guide: Get the current macro market regime from SignalFuse. GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/regime with no parameters and pay the $0.001 USDC x402 quote (Base). The 200 JSON returns regime (risk_on/risk_off/neutral), classification (bullish/bearish/neutral), confidence (0-1), a short reasoning string, and updated_at. If the signal has decayed you get regime='neutral' with confidence=0 and a 'Decayed — last signal was Nh ago' reasoning — still a valid paid 200. For per-asset entry/exit signals follow the related[] pointers to /v1/signal/{symbol}.

Observed for BTC: signal='neutral', signal_strength=55, confidence=0, regime='neutral', components.social={0.692,'positive'}, components.macro={0,'neutral'}, components.market={-0.286,'short_bias'}, stale=true.

SAME-HOST TRAP: /v1/sentiment/{symbol} on this exact host is a DIFFERENT, equity-only op (TSLA/PLTR/NVDA...) that charge-then-errors on crypto tickers (the hidden 'SignalFuse Social Sentiment' entry). /v1/signal/ is the crypto one and does work for BTC. Do not conflate them.

Freshness varies: the paid BTC response came back stale=true with data_age_seconds ~125862 (~35h old) and confidence=0 — the endpoint works and returns real structured data, but check the `stale` and `data_age_seconds` fields before trusting a signal.

Component labels observed ('positive'/'neutral'/'short_bias') differ from the 402 outputSchema example ('bullish'); the response also carries a `related` array of paid-endpoint upsell links that is not in the advertised schema.
x402 payment settles ($0.01 USDC on Base) but the runtime response reports confirmed=false and returns no txHash (consistent with other endpoints on this host).

Provider offers non-x402 fallbacks not indexed here: a trial credit token (POST /v1/credits/trial {wallet} -> 5 free credits, x-credit-token header) and a browser playground (signalfuse.co/play, 25 free calls/day). Free companion endpoints on the host: GET /v1/regime/preview, /v1/arena/leaderboard, /v1/health.
usage.guide: Get a fused directional crypto trading signal for one ticker. GET https://api.signalfuse.co/v1/signal/{symbol} with the ticker in the PATH (BTC, ETH, SOL, DOGE, PEPE, WIF, BONK, ARB, OP, or AVAX only) — no query params, no body. Pay $0.01 x402 in USDC on Base and read the result inline at 200 (synchronous, no polling). Output: symbol, signal (long|short|neutral), signal_strength (0-100), confidence (0-1), regime (risk_on|risk_off|neutral), and a components breakdown of social/macro/market {score,label}, plus updated_at, data_age_seconds and a `stale` flag — check `stale`/`data_age_seconds` before acting on the signal, as freshness varies. Do NOT use /v1/sentiment/{symbol} for crypto: that sibling op is equity-only and errors after charging.

name: Cryptyx Signal Fork
description: Fork a registered Cryptyx trading signal into a new inactive parameter variant (a fresh version id storing a custom param vector) without touching the live/production firing — the experimentation primitive to fork, dry-run backtest, then activate a tweaked signal geometry.

signal_id.description: Registered signal_id in signals.signal_registry. Uppercased before lookup (e.g., TR_MOMO_CONT_14D, VOL_COMPRESSION_7v30, FUT_FUNDING_STRESS). Required.

params.description: Non-empty JSONB parameter object stored as the new inactive version. Keys are NOT validated against the signal's param schema — the caller must supply the correct keys for the target signal's geometry (e.g., t_thr, dt_max, vol_thr). Required.

version.description: The new inactive version id created by the fork.

params.description: Echo of the stored param vector for the new version.

is_active.description: Always false for a fresh fork — production firing is untouched until a separate activate step.

created_at.description: ISO timestamp of the new version.

_next.description: Provider upsell block: recommended paid follow-up Cryptyx endpoints {path, method, price_usd, reason}. Informational, not data.

usage.callShape: POST https://cryptyx.ai/api/signals/fork with a JSON body {signal_id:'<REGISTERED_SIGNAL_ID>', params:{...}}. Both fields are required; signal_id must be a real signal in the Cryptyx registry (uppercased server-side) and params must be a non-empty object of the keys that signal's geometry expects. Settle the x402 402 challenge ($0.05 USDC on Base, eip155:8453). The new version id + stored params are returned inline in the 200 (synchronous, no poll, no API key).
usage.outputShape: JSON object: ok(bool); signal_id (echo, uppercased); version (new inactive version id, number); params (echo of the stored vector); is_active (false — production untouched); created_at (ISO ts); plus a _next upsell block. Verified paid run (signal_id TR_MOMO_CONT_14D, params {t_thr:0.55, dt_max:-0.08}) returned {ok:true, signal_id:'TR_MOMO_CONT_14D', version:196, params:{t_thr:0.55, dt_max:-0.08}, is_active:false, created_at:'2026-08-07T23:30:44.289Z'} and a _next block pointing to /api/signals/explain, /api/signals/catalog, /api/signals/top, /api/asset/thesis and /api/v1/ai/trade-ideas.
quirks: MUTATING but non-destructive: each paid call CREATES a new inactive signal version (version id increments — the same body produced version 196 on this run) and NEVER touches live/production firing. It is the 'fork' step of a fork -> dryrun-backtest -> activate workflow; a fork alone does not affect any real signal.

Both signal_id and params are required; params must be a NON-EMPTY object or the fork is rejected. signal_id is uppercased before registry lookup, so it must resolve to a real registered signal (e.g. TR_MOMO_CONT_14D, VOL_COMPRESSION_7v30, FUT_FUNDING_STRESS).

params keys are NOT validated against the target signal's param schema — the caller is responsible for supplying the correct geometry keys (e.g. t_thr, dt_max, vol_thr) for that signal; wrong keys are stored verbatim and would produce a meaningless variant.

The x402 402 challenge is delivered via the base64 `payment-required` HTTP header; the 402 response body itself is empty ({}). Accepts: a single Base (eip155:8453) USDC lane, amount 50000 (6-decimal) = $0.05, no Solana lane.
Response carries a _next upsell block referencing other paid Cryptyx endpoints (signals/explain, signals/catalog, signals/top, asset/thesis, v1/ai/trade-ideas) — ignore it as data.
